title: Hōryū-ji
summary: After a fire in 670, rebuilding at Hōryū-ji continued into the early eighth century. Surviving timber structures show adaptations of Buddhist architectural practices within the Japanese setting.

Rebuilding began after 670 and continued into the early eighth century; 725 is a coarse indexing bound for “early”, not a completion date.
The history of a religious institution is longer than that of any one building. Dating the surviving structures separately helps avoid assigning the original foundation date to later woodwork.
